sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168][F1][F10].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [D161][F5][D200][F6][D238][F7].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices [D274][P47], and the three years to FY2025 compounded at -5.3% [D844].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue and contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% growth, while natural gas added 4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D551][D553][D342][D586][D585].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude prices [P28].
The Lower 48 segment contributed 8.0pp of FY2025 growth on 11.8% growth and 70.2% of revenue, while the pipeline business subtracted 2.6pp [D713][D712][D711][D621].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against 4.9% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage [D343][D342].
Diluted EPS fell 18.7% against the 13.6% net income decline as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D345][D343][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025 and has fallen 15.2pp from the 30.6% FY2022 peak [D351][F30][F27].
FY2025 earnings fell on lower commodity prices, lower equity-affiliate earnings and higher exploration expense, partly offset by higher volumes [P12][P14].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% in FY2025 from 32.4% in FY2024, and DD&A rose to 19.5% of revenue from 17.5% [D332][D298][D330][D296].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.18x of FY2024 [F59][D333][D299].
The FY2025 decline from $20.1 billion in FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, but the pack has no free cash flow after FY2022 [D185][D834].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, the highest capex-to-D&A ratio in the window [D222][D228].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in FY2025 against a -7.7% peer median, ranking in the 100th percentile of six energy peers [D337][D338][D851][D850].

FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capital investment, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the company's greater-than-30% framework [P31][D339][F59].
The diluted share count still rose 6.1% in FY2025, so repurchases did not offset issuance [D356].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix a recast year with a first-reported year are not like-for-like, so the trend above rests on the recast series alone [R1].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023, the only decline in the last four years [F8][D274].
That drop was driven by lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P47].
A price-led decline of that size shows how much of the top line still depends on commodity prices rather than volumes [R2].
Whether net margin holds above the 15.4% FY2025 level or falls toward the 17.9% window median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F30][D831].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 12.1% FY2025 level or moves toward the -7.7% peer median, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D338][D851].
Whether the diluted share count falls below the 1,253.4 million FY2025 level or rises again, reported in the FY2026 10-K [X131].
